html:
Chuquicamata is a vast open-pit copper mine in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, opened on a large scale in 1915 by American investors. It is among the largest open-pit mines in the world.

The Guggenheim family and later the Anaconda Company used new methods to mine low-grade ore on a huge scale. As nitrate declined, copper became the main export of Chile, and Chile became the world's largest producer. American companies took much of the profit, which fed nationalist anger.

In 1971 Congress voted unanimously to nationalise the big mines under Salvador Allende, and the state company Codelco took them over in 1976. The military kept a share of copper money for the armed forces. Copper is still about half of Chile's exports, and the world demand for it, as for the lithium of the region, ties Chile to the world economy.
sum: Chuquicamata is a vast open-pit copper mine in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, opened on a large scale in 1915 by American investors. It is among the largest open-pit mines in the world.
